name: Abdus Salam
overview: Abdus Salam was a Pakistani theoretical physicist who shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for the electroweak unification theory. He was the first Pakistani and the first Muslim to receive a Nobel Prize in science.

name: Abraham Lincoln
overview: Abraham Lincoln was the 16th President of the United States who preserved the Union during the Civil War and abolished slavery through the Emancipation Proclamation.

name: Ada Lovelace
overview: Ada Lovelace was a British mathematician and writer, recognized as the first computer programmer for her work on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine.

name: Ada Yonath
overview: Ada Yonath is an Israeli crystallographer who won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for studies of the structure and function of the ribosome.

name: Adam Smith
overview: Adam Smith was a Scottish economist and philosopher who is considered the father of modern economics and author of The Wealth of Nations.

name: Adi Shankara
overview: Adi Shankara was an Indian philosopher who consolidated the doctrine of Advaita Vedanta (non-dualism).

name: Adrien-Marie Legendre
overview: Legendre made major contributions to number theory, statistics, and analysis, including the method of least squares.

name: Aeschylus
overview: Aeschylus is the father of Greek tragedy, introducing dialogue between characters and reducing the role of the chorus.

name: Aesop
overview: Aesop was a legendary Greek fabulist credited with a collection of fables that have become a foundation of Western moral literature.

name: Ahmad Shah Durrani
overview: Ahmad Shah Durrani was the founder of the Durrani Empire and is considered the father of modern Afghanistan.

name: Ahmed Zewail
overview: Ahmed Zewail was an Egyptian-American chemist who won the Nobel Prize for his pioneering work in femtochemistry, the study of chemical reactions at extremely short timescales.

name: Ai Weiwei
overview: Ai Weiwei is a Chinese contemporary artist and activist known for his architectural, sculptural, and social media work that challenges authority.

name: Akbar the Great
overview: Akbar the Great was the third Mughal Emperor who expanded the empire across most of the Indian subcontinent and promoted religious tolerance.

name: Al-Farabi
overview: Al-Farabi was a renowned Islamic philosopher and polymath known as the Second Teacher after Aristotle. He made major contributions to political philosophy, logic, and music theory.

name: Al-Ghazali
overview: Al-Ghazali was a Persian theologian, philosopher, and mystic who profoundly influenced Islamic thought. His critique of philosophy and embrace of Sufism reshaped the Islamic intellectual tradition.

name: Al-Khwarizmi
overview: Al-Khwarizmi was a Persian mathematician and astronomer whose works introduced Hindu-Arabic numerals and algebra to Europe.

name: Alan Kay
overview: Alan Kay is an American computer scientist known for his pioneering work on object-oriented programming, personal computing, and graphical user interfaces.

name: Alan Turing
overview: Alan Turing was a British mathematician and computer scientist who formalized the concepts of algorithm and computation with the Turing machine. He played a crucial role in breaking the Enigma code during World War II.

name: Albert Camus
overview: Albert Camus was a French-Algerian philosopher and author who explored absurdism, the conflict between human desire for meaning and the universe's indifference.

name: Albert Einstein
overview: Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist who developed the theory of relativity, one of the two pillars of modern physics. His work on the photoelectric effect earned him the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921. He is widely regarded as one of the most influential scientists of all time.

name: Albert Sabin
overview: Albert Sabin was a Polish-American medical researcher who developed the oral polio vaccine that became the primary tool in the global eradication of poliomyelitis.

name: Albert Schweitzer
overview: Albert Schweitzer was an Alsatian-German theologian, philosopher, musician, and physician who devoted his life to medical missionary work in Africa.

name: Albrecht Dürer
overview: Albrecht Dürer was a German painter, printmaker, and theorist of the German Renaissance, known for his high-quality woodcuts and engravings.

name: Alexander Blok
overview: Alexander Blok was a leading Russian Symbolist poet whose work captured the mysticism and upheaval of early 20th-century Russia.

name: Dmitri Mendeleev's Teacher Aleksandr Butlerov
overview: Aleksandr Butlerov was a Russian chemist who was one of the principal creators of the theory of chemical structure and the first to introduce the term.

name: Alessandro Volta
overview: Alessandro Volta was an Italian physicist and chemist who invented the voltaic pile, the first true electric battery, providing the first reliable source of continuous electric current. The volt, the SI unit of electric potential, is named in his honor.

name: Alexander Fleming
overview: Alexander Fleming was a Scottish physician and microbiologist who discovered penicillin, the world's first broadly effective antibiotic.

name: Alexander Graham Bell
overview: Alexander Graham Bell was a Scottish-born inventor, scientist, and engineer who is credited with patenting the first practical telephone.

name: Alexander Grothendieck
overview: Alexander Grothendieck was a German-born French mathematician who revolutionized algebraic geometry and is considered one of the greatest mathematicians of the 20th century.

name: Alexander Prokhorov
overview: Alexander Prokhorov co-developed the theoretical basis for the maser and laser.

name: Alexander Pushkin
overview: Alexander Pushkin was a Russian poet and novelist who is considered the founder of modern Russian literature. His verse novel Eugene Onegin is a masterpiece of world literature.

name: Alexander the Great
overview: Alexander the Great was a king of Macedonia who created one of the largest empires in ancient history, stretching from Greece to northwestern India.

name: Alexander von Humboldt
overview: Alexander von Humboldt was a Prussian naturalist and explorer whose quantitative work on botanical geography laid the foundation for biogeography and ecology.

name: Alexis de Tocqueville
overview: Alexis de Tocqueville was a French political thinker and historian whose Democracy in America remains the most penetrating analysis of American democratic society ever written.

name: Alfred Kinsey
overview: Alfred Kinsey was an American biologist and professor of entomology and zoology who founded the Institute for Sex Research at Indiana University.

name: Alfred Nobel
overview: Alfred Nobel was a Swedish chemist, engineer, inventor, and businessman, best known for inventing dynamite and for establishing the Nobel Prizes.

name: Alfred North Whitehead
overview: Alfred North Whitehead was a British mathematician and philosopher who co-authored Principia Mathematica with Bertrand Russell and later developed process philosophy.

name: Alfred Russel Wallace
overview: Alfred Russel Wallace was a British naturalist who independently conceived the theory of evolution through natural selection, prompting Darwin to publish his own theory.

name: Alfred the Great
overview: Alfred the Great was King of Wessex who defended England against the Vikings and promoted learning and law.

name: Alfred Wegener
overview: Alfred Wegener was a German meteorologist and geophysicist who proposed the theory of continental drift.

name: Alfred Werner
overview: Alfred Werner was a Swiss chemist who won the Nobel Prize for proposing the octahedral configuration of transition metal complexes, founding coordination chemistry.

name: Allen Ginsberg
overview: Allen Ginsberg was a Beat poet whose Howl became a landmark of American countercultural literature.

name: Alonzo Church
overview: Alonzo Church was an American mathematician and logician who made major contributions to mathematical logic and theoretical computer science.

name: Ambroise Pare
overview: Ambroise Pare was a French barber-surgeon who is considered the father of modern surgery for his revolutionary techniques in wound treatment and surgical practice.

name: Amedeo Avogadro
overview: Amedeo Avogadro was an Italian scientist known for his contribution to molecular theory, including what is now known as Avogadro's law and Avogadro's number.

name: Amina of Zaria
overview: Queen Amina was a warrior queen of the Hausa city-state of Zazzau (Zaria) in present-day Nigeria, celebrated for her military conquests and fortification-building.

name: Amy Tan
overview: Amy Tan is a Chinese-American novelist best known for The Joy Luck Club.

name: Andre-Marie Ampere
overview: Andre-Marie Ampere was a French physicist and mathematician who was one of the founders of the science of classical electromagnetism. He formulated Ampere's law and is considered the father of electrodynamics; the ampere unit of electric current is named after him.

name: André Weil
overview: André Weil was one of the most influential mathematicians of the 20th century and a founding member of the Bourbaki group.

name: Andreas Vesalius
overview: Andreas Vesalius was a Flemish anatomist and physician who is considered the founder of modern human anatomy.

name: Andrei Platonov
overview: Andrei Platonov was a Russian writer whose deeply original prose explored the contradictions of Soviet utopianism.

name: Andrei Sakharov
overview: Andrei Sakharov was a Soviet nuclear physicist who played a key role in developing the Soviet hydrogen bomb and later became a prominent human rights activist. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1975 for his courageous advocacy for disarmament and civil liberties.

name: Andrew Wiles
overview: Andrew Wiles is a British mathematician who proved Fermat's Last Theorem in 1995, solving a problem that had been open for 358 years.

name: Andrey Kolmogorov
overview: Andrey Kolmogorov was a Soviet mathematician who made fundamental contributions to probability theory, topology, turbulence, and algorithmic complexity.

name: Andy Warhol
overview: Andy Warhol was an American artist, film director, and producer who was a leading figure in the Pop Art movement.

name: Anish Kapoor
overview: Anish Kapoor is an Indian-born British sculptor known for his monumental works that play with form, color, and the perception of space.

name: Anna Akhmatova
overview: Anna Akhmatova was one of the most significant Russian poets of the 20th century, whose work bore witness to the Stalinist terror.

name: Annie Jump Cannon
overview: Annie Jump Cannon was an American astronomer who classified the spectra of hundreds of thousands of stars, creating the Harvard spectral classification system still used today.

name: Ansel Adams
overview: Ansel Adams was an American landscape photographer and environmentalist known for his black-and-white photographs of the American West.

name: Henri Becquerel
overview: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity, opening a new field of physics.

name: Antoine Lavoisier
overview: Antoine Lavoisier was a French nobleman and chemist who is considered the father of modern chemistry. He named oxygen and hydrogen, helped construct the metric system, and wrote the first extensive list of elements.

name: Anton Chekhov
overview: Anton Chekhov was a Russian playwright and short-story writer regarded as one of the greatest short-story writers in history. His plays revolutionized modern drama.

name: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek
overview: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was a Dutch businessman and scientist, often called the father of microbiology. He was the first to observe bacteria and protozoa using microscopes he built himself.

name: Antonín Dvořák
overview: Antonín Dvořák was a Czech composer known for integrating folk music elements into the classical tradition, creating music of distinctive national character.

name: Antonio Vivaldi
overview: Antonio Vivaldi was an Italian Baroque composer, virtuoso violinist, and priest, famous for his concertos, especially The Four Seasons.

name: Anwar Sadat
overview: Anwar Sadat was the President of Egypt who made the historic peace with Israel, winning the Nobel Peace Prize and fundamentally altering Middle Eastern politics.

name: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
overview: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was India's Missile Man and 11th President, who led the development of India's ballistic missile and nuclear weapons programs.

name: Archibald Scott Couper
overview: Archibald Scott Couper was a Scottish chemist who proposed that carbon atoms can link to each other to form chains, independently of Kekulé, laying groundwork for structural chemistry.

name: Archimedes
overview: Archimedes of Syracuse was an ancient Greek mathematician, physicist, engineer, and astronomer, widely regarded as one of the greatest scientists of antiquity. He made groundbreaking contributions to geometry, statics, hydrostatics, and the design of innovative machines.

name: Aretha Franklin
overview: Aretha Franklin was an American singer, songwriter, and pianist known as the 'Queen of Soul,' celebrated for her powerful vocals and emotional intensity.

name: Aristophanes
overview: Aristophanes was the greatest comic playwright of ancient Athens, known for sharp political satire and imaginative fantasy.

name: Aristotle
overview: Aristotle was an ancient Greek philosopher and polymath whose writings cover physics, biology, metaphysics, logic, ethics, and politics. He was Plato's student and Alexander the Great's tutor.

name: Artemisia Gentileschi
overview: Artemisia Gentileschi was an Italian Baroque painter who was one of the most accomplished painters of the early Baroque era and the first woman admitted to the Accademia del Disegno.

name: Arthur Compton
overview: Arthur Compton was an American physicist who demonstrated that X-rays and gamma rays have particle-like properties through the Compton scattering effect. His work provided key evidence for the quantum nature of electromagnetic radiation. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1927.

name: Arthur Rimbaud
overview: Arthur Rimbaud was a French poet who influenced modern literature and the Surrealist movement.

name: Arthur Rubinstein
overview: Arthur Rubinstein was a Polish-American pianist celebrated as one of the greatest interpreters of Chopin and the Romantic repertoire.

name: Arthur Schopenhauer
overview: Arthur Schopenhauer was a German philosopher best known for his work The World as Will and Representation, which characterized the phenomenal world as driven by a blind, purposeless will.

name: Aryabhata
overview: Aryabhata was an Indian mathematician and astronomer who made groundbreaking contributions to both fields.

name: Ashoka the Great
overview: Ashoka was an Indian emperor of the Maurya Dynasty who is considered one of the greatest rulers in history for his embrace of Buddhism and nonviolence.

name: August Kekulé
overview: August Kekulé was a German organic chemist who was the principal founder of the theory of chemical structure, including the structure of benzene as a ring.

name: Auguste Comte
overview: Auguste Comte was a French philosopher who founded positivism and sociology, establishing the scientific study of society as an academic discipline.

name: Pierre-Auguste Renoir
overview: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter known for his vibrant light, saturated color, and celebration of beauty, especially of the human figure.

name: Auguste Rodin
overview: Auguste Rodin was a French sculptor generally considered the founder of modern sculpture, breaking with traditional decorative traditions.

name: Augustin-Jean Fresnel
overview: Augustin-Jean Fresnel was a French civil engineer and physicist who made major contributions to the wave theory of light. He developed the mathematical framework for diffraction and polarization, and invented the Fresnel lens used in lighthouses worldwide.

name: Augustin-Louis Cauchy
overview: Augustin-Louis Cauchy was a French mathematician who pioneered rigorous foundations of calculus and made fundamental contributions to complex analysis and group theory.

name: Augustine of Hippo
overview: Augustine of Hippo was a theologian and philosopher who profoundly shaped Western Christianity and philosophy. His Confessions is considered the first Western autobiography.

name: Augusto Cesar Sandino
overview: Augusto Cesar Sandino was a Nicaraguan revolutionary who led a guerrilla war against the United States occupation of Nicaragua.

name: Augustus
overview: Augustus was the first Roman emperor, founding the Roman Principate and transforming the Republic into an empire that would endure for centuries.

name: Aung San Suu Kyi
overview: Aung San Suu Kyi is a Myanmar politician and Nobel laureate who spent years under house arrest for her pro-democracy activism before leading the government.

name: Aung San
overview: Aung San was the founder of modern Burma (Myanmar) and the chief architect of Burmese independence.

name: Averroes
overview: Averroes (Ibn Rushd) was an Andalusian-Arab philosopher and jurist who wrote extensive commentaries on Aristotle, earning him the title 'The Commentator' in medieval Europe.

name: Avicenna
overview: Avicenna (Ibn Sina) was a Persian polymath regarded as one of the most significant thinkers of the Islamic Golden Age. He made major contributions to philosophy, medicine, and science.

name: Banana Yoshimoto
overview: Banana Yoshimoto is a Japanese writer known for her fiction exploring themes of death, loss, and healing with gentle, dreamlike prose.

name: Banksy
overview: Banksy is an anonymous England-based street artist, political activist, and film director whose satirical street art combines dark humor with social commentary.

name: Barbara McClintock
overview: Barbara McClintock was an American cytogeneticist who was awarded the Nobel Prize for her discovery of genetic transposition, or 'jumping genes.'

name: Emmy Noether's student Bartel Leendert van der Waerden
overview: B.L. van der Waerden was a Dutch mathematician who transformed algebra through his influential textbook Moderne Algebra.

name: Baruch Spinoza
overview: Baruch Spinoza was a Dutch philosopher of Sephardic Jewish origin whose Ethics is one of the greatest works of Western philosophy. He developed a rationalist metaphysical system equating God with Nature.

name: Béla Bartók
overview: Béla Bartók was a Hungarian composer and pianist, one of the founders of ethnomusicology and one of the most important composers of the 20th century.

name: Ben Jonson
overview: Ben Jonson was a major English playwright and poet, Shakespeare's chief rival, who championed classical dramatic principles.

name: Benazir Bhutto
overview: Benazir Bhutto was the first woman to head a democratic government in a Muslim-majority country.

name: Benedetto Croce
overview: Benedetto Croce was an Italian idealist philosopher, historian, and prominent anti-fascist intellectual.

name: Benito Juárez
overview: Benito Juárez was a Mexican lawyer and politician who served as President of Mexico and is regarded as the country's greatest and most beloved leader.

name: Benjamin Disraeli
overview: Benjamin Disraeli was a British Prime Minister and novelist who expanded the British Empire and enacted social reforms.

name: Benjamin Franklin
overview: Benjamin Franklin was an American polymath, statesman, and one of the Founding Fathers of the United States. As a scientist, he is best known for his experiments with electricity, including the famous kite experiment, and for inventing the lightning rod.

name: Bernardo O'Higgins
overview: Bernardo O'Higgins was the Chilean independence leader and first Supreme Director of Chile, known as the 'Father of the Nation.'

name: Bernhard Riemann
overview: Bernhard Riemann was a German mathematician who made lasting contributions to analysis, number theory, and differential geometry. His work laid the mathematical foundation for general relativity.

name: Bertrand Russell
overview: Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher, logician, and mathematician who co-authored Principia Mathematica and made major contributions to mathematical logic and analytic philosophy.

name: Billie Holiday
overview: Billie Holiday was an American jazz singer whose vocal style, influenced by jazz instrumentalists, pioneered a new way of manipulating phrasing and tempo.

name: Biruté Galdikas
overview: Biruté Galdikas is a Lithuanian-Canadian primatologist who is the world's foremost authority on orangutans.

name: Blaise Pascal
overview: Blaise Pascal was a French mathematician, physicist, and philosopher who made fundamental contributions to projective geometry, probability theory, and the physics of fluids and pressure.

name: Blaise Pascal
overview: Blaise Pascal was a French mathematician, physicist, inventor, and philosopher. He made fundamental contributions to projective geometry, probability theory, and fluid mechanics, and invented one of the earliest mechanical calculators.

name: Bob Dylan
overview: Bob Dylan is an American singer-songwriter who has been a major figure in popular culture for more than 60 years, winning the Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Bob Marley
overview: Bob Marley was a Jamaican singer-songwriter who became an international musical and cultural icon through his reggae music.

name: Boethius
overview: Boethius wrote The Consolation of Philosophy, one of the most widely read books of the Middle Ages.

name: Boris Pasternak
overview: Boris Pasternak was a Russian poet and novelist best known for Doctor Zhivago, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: B.R. Ambedkar
overview: B.R. Ambedkar was the chief architect of the Indian Constitution and a champion of the rights of Dalits.

name: Brahmagupta
overview: Brahmagupta was an Indian mathematician and astronomer who was the first to formalize arithmetic rules for zero and negative numbers and made major contributions to algebra.

name: Brothers Grimm
overview: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected and published German fairy tales and pioneered German linguistics.

name: Georges-Louis Leclerc, Comte de Buffon
overview: The Comte de Buffon was a French naturalist whose encyclopedic work Histoire Naturelle was one of the first attempts to describe the natural world comprehensively.

name: Burton Richter
overview: Burton Richter was an American physicist who co-discovered the J/psi meson, providing evidence for the charm quark.

name: C.V. Raman
overview: C.V. Raman was an Indian physicist who discovered the Raman effect, the inelastic scattering of light, winning the Nobel Prize.

name: Camillo Benso, Count of Cavour
overview: Cavour was the architect of Italian unification who served as the first Prime Minister of a united Italy.

name: Cao Xueqin
overview: Cao Xueqin was a Chinese novelist and author of Dream of the Red Chamber, one of China's Four Great Classical Novels and one of the greatest novels in world literature.

name: Caravaggio
overview: Caravaggio was an Italian painter whose revolutionary use of dramatic lighting and realistic figures transformed European painting in the Baroque period.

name: Carl Bosch
overview: Carl Bosch was a German chemist and engineer who won the Nobel Prize for contributions to the invention and development of chemical high-pressure methods, including the Haber-Bosch process.

name: Carl David Anderson
overview: Carl David Anderson was an American experimental physicist who discovered the positron, the first known antimatter particle, in 1932. He also co-discovered the muon in 1936, and was awarded the 1936 Nobel Prize in Physics for the positron discovery.

name: Carl Djerassi
overview: Carl Djerassi was an Austrian-American chemist and author who is best known as the father of the birth control pill.

name: Carl Friedrich Gauss
overview: Carl Friedrich Gauss was a German mathematician and physicist who made extraordinary contributions to number theory, algebra, statistics, analysis, and astronomy. He is often called the Prince of Mathematicians.

name: Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi
overview: Carl Jacobi was a German mathematician who made fundamental contributions to elliptic functions, dynamics, differential equations, and number theory.

name: Carl Linnaeus
overview: Carl Linnaeus was a Swedish botanist, zoologist, and physician who formalized binomial nomenclature, the modern system of naming organisms.

name: Carl Sagan
overview: Carl Sagan was an American astronomer, planetary scientist, and science communicator who became one of the most well-known scientists in the world.

name: Carl Wieman
overview: Carl Wieman co-produced the first true Bose-Einstein condensate and later became a leader in physics education.

name: Carl Wilhelm Scheele
overview: Carl Wilhelm Scheele was a Swedish-German pharmaceutical chemist who discovered oxygen independently of Priestley, as well as chlorine, manganese, and several organic acids.

name: Carlo Rubbia
overview: Carlo Rubbia is an Italian particle physicist who led the experiments that discovered the W and Z bosons, confirming the electroweak theory.

name: Caroline Herschel
overview: Caroline Herschel was a German-born British astronomer who was the first woman to discover a comet and the first woman to receive a salary as a scientist.

name: Catherine the Great
overview: Catherine the Great was Empress of Russia whose reign is considered the Golden Age of Russia, marked by territorial expansion and cultural development.

name: Catullus
overview: Catullus was a Roman lyric poet whose passionate, personal verse influenced all subsequent Western love poetry.

name: Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin
overview: Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin was a British-American astronomer who first proposed that stars are composed primarily of hydrogen and helium.

name: César Vallejo
overview: César Vallejo was a Peruvian poet regarded as one of the great poetic innovators of the 20th century.

name: Cesare Beccaria
overview: Cesare Beccaria was an Italian Enlightenment thinker whose work On Crimes and Punishments laid the foundation for modern criminal justice reform.

name: Cetshwayo kaMpande
overview: Cetshwayo was the last great king of the independent Zulu Kingdom who inflicted a devastating defeat on the British at the Battle of Isandlwana.

name: Chandragupta Maurya
overview: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire, the first empire to unify most of the Indian subcontinent.

name: Charlemagne
overview: Charlemagne was King of the Franks and Lombards and Emperor of the Romans who united most of Western Europe for the first time since the Roman Empire.

name: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb
overview: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb was a French military engineer and physicist who is best known for formulating Coulomb's law, which describes the electrostatic force between charged particles. His torsion balance experiments established the quantitative foundations of electrostatics.

name: Charles Babbage
overview: Charles Babbage was an English polymath who originated the concept of a digital programmable computer with his Difference Engine and Analytical Engine designs.

name: Charles Baudelaire
overview: Charles Baudelaire was a French poet who pioneered symbolism and modern poetry.

name: Charles Darwin
overview: Charles Darwin was an English naturalist who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection, fundamentally changing our understanding of life on Earth.

name: Charles de Gaulle
overview: Charles de Gaulle was a French general who led the Free French during WWII and founded the Fifth Republic as its first president.

name: Charles Dickens
overview: Charles Dickens was an English novelist and social critic who created some of the world's best-known fictional characters. He is regarded as the greatest novelist of the Victorian era.

name: Charles Hermite
overview: Charles Hermite was a French mathematician who proved the transcendence of e and made important contributions to number theory, algebra, and analysis.

name: Charles Lyell
overview: Charles Lyell was a British geologist whose Principles of Geology influenced Darwin's thinking and established uniformitarianism as the basis of geology.

name: Charles Townes
overview: Charles Townes invented the maser and contributed fundamental work leading to the laser.

name: Charlie Parker
overview: Charlie Parker was an American jazz saxophonist and composer who was a leading figure in the development of bebop.

name: Che Guevara
overview: Ernesto 'Che' Guevara was an Argentine Marxist revolutionary who was a major figure of the Cuban Revolution and became a symbol of rebellion worldwide.

name: Chen-Ning Yang
overview: Chen-Ning Yang is a Chinese-American theoretical physicist who shared the 1957 Nobel Prize in Physics for the prediction of parity violation. He is also renowned for the Yang-Mills theory, which became the foundation of the Standard Model of particle physics.

name: Wangari Maathai's contemporary Chico Mendes
overview: Chico Mendes was a Brazilian rubber tapper, trade union leader, and environmentalist who fought to preserve the Amazon rainforest.

name: Chien-Shiung Wu
overview: Chien-Shiung Wu was a Chinese-American experimental physicist known for conducting the Wu experiment, which proved that parity is not conserved in weak interactions. Often called the 'First Lady of Physics,' she made fundamental contributions to nuclear and particle physics.

name: Chikamatsu Monzaemon
overview: Chikamatsu Monzaemon is considered the greatest dramatist in Japanese literature, often called the 'Shakespeare of Japan' for his bunraku puppet plays and kabuki works.

name: Chinua Achebe
overview: Chinua Achebe was a Nigerian novelist whose Things Fall Apart is the most widely read book in modern African literature. He is considered the father of African literature in English.

name: Christiaan Barnard
overview: Christiaan Barnard was a South African cardiac surgeon who performed the world's first successful human-to-human heart transplant.

name: Christiaan Huygens
overview: Christiaan Huygens was a Dutch mathematician, physicist, and astronomer who was one of the leading scientists of the 17th century. He proposed the wave theory of light, invented the pendulum clock, and discovered Saturn's largest moon, Titan.

name: Christo
overview: Christo was a Bulgarian-born American artist known for massive environmental works of art created with his wife Jeanne-Claude.

name: Christoph Scheiner
overview: Christoph Scheiner was a Jesuit astronomer who independently discovered sunspots and made detailed studies of solar phenomena.

name: Christoph Willibald Gluck
overview: Gluck reformed opera by emphasizing dramatic expression over vocal display, paving the way for Mozart and Wagner.

name: Christopher Wren
overview: Christopher Wren was England's greatest architect, who redesigned London after the Great Fire and built St Paul's Cathedral.

name: Marcus Tullius Cicero
overview: Cicero was Rome's greatest orator and a pivotal figure in transmitting Greek philosophy to the Latin-speaking world.

name: Cindy Sherman
overview: Cindy Sherman is an American photographer and film director known for her conceptual self-portraits exploring identity and representation.

name: Clara Schumann
overview: Clara Schumann was a German pianist and composer, one of the most distinguished pianists of the Romantic era and one of the first professional female concert pianists.

name: Claude Debussy
overview: Claude Debussy was a French composer who developed a new approach to harmony and orchestration that became known as musical Impressionism.

name: Claude Levi-Strauss
overview: Claude Levi-Strauss was a French anthropologist who founded structural anthropology and transformed the understanding of human cultures through the analysis of myths, kinship, and classification systems.

name: Claude Monet
overview: Claude Monet was a French painter and founder of Impressionism, known for his revolutionary approach to capturing light and atmosphere in paint.

name: Claude Shannon
overview: Claude Shannon was an American mathematician, electrical engineer, and cryptographer known as the father of information theory.

name: Clement Attlee
overview: Clement Attlee was a British Prime Minister who built the welfare state, including the National Health Service.

name: Cleopatra VII
overview: Cleopatra VII was the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt, known for her intelligence, political acumen, and alliances with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony.

name: C.N.R. Rao
overview: C.N.R. Rao is one of the world's foremost solid-state and materials chemists, with pioneering work on transition metal oxides and nanomaterials.

name: Confucius
overview: Confucius was a Chinese philosopher and teacher whose ideas on ethics, family, and governance profoundly shaped East Asian civilization. His teachings form the basis of Confucianism.

name: Corazon Aquino
overview: Corazon Aquino was the first female President of the Philippines who led the People Power Revolution that peacefully overthrew the Marcos dictatorship.

name: Craig Venter
overview: Craig Venter is an American biotechnologist who led the private effort to sequence the human genome and later created the first synthetic cell.

name: C.V. Raman
overview: Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman was an Indian physicist who discovered the Raman effect, in which light changes wavelength when scattered by molecules. This discovery earned him the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics, making him the first Asian to receive a Nobel Prize in science.

name: Cyrus McCormick
overview: Cyrus McCormick was an American inventor and businessman who developed the mechanical reaper, transforming agriculture worldwide.

name: Cyrus the Great
overview: Cyrus the Great was the founder of the Achaemenid Empire, the first Persian Empire, and is known for his respect for the customs and religions of conquered peoples.

name: 14th Dalai Lama
overview: The 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, is the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism who has advocated for Tibetan autonomy and promoted nonviolence, winning the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Damien Hirst
overview: Damien Hirst is a British artist and the most prominent member of the Young British Artists, known for works exploring death and mortality.

name: Daniel Bernoulli
overview: Daniel Bernoulli was a Swiss mathematician and physicist best known for his work in fluid dynamics. His most important contribution, Bernoulli's principle, describes the relationship between fluid speed and pressure, forming a cornerstone of aerodynamics.

name: Daniel Defoe
overview: Daniel Defoe was an English writer and journalist, widely considered a founder of the English novel.

name: Dante Alighieri
overview: Dante Alighieri was an Italian poet whose Divine Comedy is considered one of the greatest works of world literature and the preeminent work of Italian literature.

name: Darius the Great
overview: Darius I was the third king of the Achaemenid Empire who reorganized it into the largest empire the world had yet seen.

name: Diego Rivera's contemporary David Alfaro Siqueiros
overview: David Alfaro Siqueiros was a Mexican social realist painter and one of the three great Mexican muralists alongside Rivera and Orozco.

name: David Ben-Gurion
overview: David Ben-Gurion was the primary founder of the State of Israel and its first Prime Minister.

name: David Bohm
overview: David Bohm was an American-British theoretical physicist who made important contributions to quantum mechanics, neuropsychology, and the philosophy of mind. He is best known for his alternative interpretation of quantum mechanics, the de Broglie-Bohm theory, which provides a deterministic framework for quantum phenomena.

name: David Bowie
overview: David Bowie was a British singer-songwriter and actor who was a leading figure in the music industry for over five decades, known for his reinventive approach.

name: David Hilbert
overview: David Hilbert was a German mathematician and one of the most influential mathematicians of the 19th and 20th centuries. He formulated 23 unsolved problems that guided mathematical research for decades.

name: David Hume
overview: David Hume was a Scottish philosopher, historian, and economist who is considered one of the most important figures in Western philosophy. He advanced empiricism and skepticism.

name: David Lloyd George
overview: David Lloyd George was a British Prime Minister who led the country through the latter half of World War I and introduced pioneering social reforms.

name: David Wineland
overview: David Wineland pioneered techniques for trapping and manipulating individual ions with laser light.

name: Democritus
overview: Democritus developed the atomic theory of the universe, proposing that all matter is composed of indivisible atoms.

name: Deng Xiaoping
overview: Deng Xiaoping was a Chinese politician who led China's economic reforms and opening up, transforming it into a global economic power.

name: Denis Diderot
overview: Denis Diderot was a French Enlightenment philosopher and chief editor of the Encyclopedie, one of the most ambitious intellectual projects in history.

name: Dennis Ritchie
overview: Dennis Ritchie was an American computer scientist who created the C programming language and co-developed the Unix operating system.

name: Derek Walcott
overview: Derek Walcott was a Saint Lucian poet and playwright who won the Nobel Prize in Literature for his luminous, multicultural body of work.

name: Desmond Tutu
overview: Desmond Tutu was a South African Anglican cleric and theologian who was a leading voice against apartheid and won the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Dian Fossey
overview: Dian Fossey was an American primatologist and conservationist who dedicated her life to studying and protecting mountain gorillas in Rwanda.

name: Diego Rivera
overview: Diego Rivera was a Mexican muralist whose large-scale public murals helped establish the Mexican muralism movement and brought art to the masses.

name: Diego Velázquez
overview: Diego Velázquez was a Spanish painter who was the leading artist of the Spanish Golden Age and one of the most important painters in Western art history.

name: Diogenes of Sinope
overview: Diogenes of Sinope was the most famous Cynic philosopher, known for living in extreme simplicity.

name: Diogenes of Sinope
overview: Diogenes of Sinope was the most famous Cynic philosopher, advocating a life of virtue in accordance with nature.

name: Dizzy Gillespie
overview: Dizzy Gillespie was an American jazz trumpeter, bandleader, composer, and singer who was one of the founding figures of bebop.

name: Dmitri Mendeleev
overview: Dmitri Mendeleev was a Russian chemist and inventor who formulated the Periodic Law and created a farsighted version of the periodic table of elements.

name: Dmitri Shostakovich
overview: Dmitri Shostakovich was a Russian composer who is regarded as one of the major composers of the 20th century, navigating art and survival under Soviet repression.

name: Dom Pedro I
overview: Dom Pedro I was the founder and first Emperor of Brazil who declared the country's independence from Portugal in 1822.

name: Domenico Scarlatti
overview: Domenico Scarlatti was an Italian composer who spent most of his career in Spain, famous for his 555 keyboard sonatas.

name: Donatello
overview: Donatello was the greatest sculptor of the early Renaissance, whose works revived classical forms with unprecedented naturalism.

name: Donna Strickland
overview: Donna Strickland is a Canadian optical physicist who co-invented chirped pulse amplification (CPA), a technique for creating ultra-short, high-intensity laser pulses. She shared the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physics, becoming the third woman to receive the prize.

name: Dorothea Lange
overview: Dorothea Lange was an American documentary photographer best known for her Depression-era work for the Farm Security Administration.

name: Dorothy Hodgkin
overview: Dorothy Hodgkin was a British chemist who advanced the technique of X-ray crystallography to determine the three-dimensional structures of biomolecules, winning the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

name: Dorothy Vaughan
overview: Dorothy Vaughan was an American mathematician and computer programmer who was one of the first African American supervisors at NACA (later NASA).

name: Du Fu
overview: Du Fu was a Chinese poet of the Tang dynasty, known as the Poet-Sage. His socially conscious poetry is considered among the greatest in the Chinese literary tradition.

name: Duke Ellington
overview: Duke Ellington was an American composer, pianist, and bandleader who led his jazz orchestra for over 50 years, composing thousands of works.

name: Duns Scotus
overview: Duns Scotus was a Franciscan philosopher-theologian known for his subtle and rigorous arguments.

name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
overview: Dwight Eisenhower was the Supreme Allied Commander in WWII and the 34th President of the United States.

name: Edgar Allan Poe
overview: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer and poet who pioneered the detective fiction and horror genres. His dark, atmospheric tales and poems remain among the most popular in English literature.

name: Edgar Degas
overview: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist artist famous for his paintings, sculptures, and drawings of ballet dancers, racing scenes, and modern life.

name: Edmund Husserl
overview: Edmund Husserl was a German philosopher who founded phenomenology, the study of structures of consciousness as experienced from the first-person point of view.

name: Edmund Spenser
overview: Edmund Spenser was one of the greatest English poets, whose allegorical epic The Faerie Queene influenced English verse for centuries.

name: Édouard Manet
overview: Édouard Manet was a French modernist painter who was one of the first 19th-century artists to paint modern life and a pivotal figure in the transition from Realism to Impressionism.

name: Edvard Munch
overview: Edvard Munch was a Norwegian painter whose intensely evocative treatment of psychological themes built upon Symbolism and greatly influenced German Expressionism.

name: Edward Jenner
overview: Edward Jenner was an English physician and scientist who pioneered the concept of vaccines, developing the first smallpox vaccine.

name: Edward O. Wilson
overview: Edward O. Wilson was an American biologist and naturalist known as the father of sociobiology and a champion of biodiversity conservation.

name: Edward Teller
overview: Edward Teller was a Hungarian-American theoretical physicist known as the 'father of the hydrogen bomb.' He made important contributions to nuclear and molecular physics, spectroscopy, and surface physics.

name: Edward Witten
overview: Edward Witten is an American theoretical physicist and mathematician widely regarded as one of the most brilliant physicists of his generation. He is the leading figure in string theory and proposed M-theory, which unified the five consistent superstring theories.

name: Edwin Hubble
overview: Edwin Hubble was an American astronomer who played a crucial role in establishing the field of extragalactic astronomy and demonstrated that the universe is expanding.

name: Egon Schiele
overview: Egon Schiele was an Austrian Expressionist painter notable for his raw sexuality, distorted body shapes, and emotional intensity.

name: El Greco
overview: El Greco was a Greek painter, sculptor, and architect of the Spanish Renaissance whose visionary style anticipated Expressionism by centuries.

name: Eleanor Roosevelt
overview: Eleanor Roosevelt was an American political figure, diplomat, and activist who served as First Lady and later as a UN delegate championing human rights.

name: Eli Whitney
overview: Eli Whitney was an American inventor who created the cotton gin and pioneered the concept of interchangeable parts in manufacturing.

name: Élie Cartan
overview: Élie Cartan was a French mathematician who made fundamental contributions to differential geometry, Lie groups, and the theory of spinors.

name: Elizabeth Blackwell
overview: Elizabeth Blackwell was the first woman to receive a medical degree in the United States, breaking the gender barrier in Western medicine.

name: Elizabeth I
overview: Elizabeth I was Queen of England and Ireland whose 45-year reign is considered a golden age of English history, with the flowering of arts and exploration.

name: Ella Fitzgerald
overview: Ella Fitzgerald was an American jazz singer known as the 'First Lady of Song,' celebrated for her purity of tone, impeccable diction, and phrasing.

name: Emil Fischer
overview: Emil Fischer was a German chemist who won the Nobel Prize for his work on sugar and purine syntheses. He is considered the founder of biochemistry.

name: Émile Borel
overview: Émile Borel was a French mathematician who made important contributions to measure theory, probability, and game theory. He was a pioneer of modern probability theory.

name: Emile Durkheim
overview: Emile Durkheim was a French sociologist who established sociology as a formal academic discipline and developed the concept of social facts.

name: Émile Picard
overview: Émile Picard made important contributions to analysis and algebraic geometry.

name: Emiliano Zapata
overview: Emiliano Zapata was a leading figure in the Mexican Revolution who championed agrarian reform and the rights of Mexico's indigenous peasants.

name: Emilie du Chatelet
overview: Emilie du Chatelet was a French natural philosopher, mathematician, and physicist who made significant contributions to Newtonian mechanics. Her translation and commentary on Newton's Principia Mathematica remains the standard French translation, and she proposed the concept of kinetic energy as proportional to the square of velocity.

name: Emilio Aguinaldo
overview: Emilio Aguinaldo was the first president of the Philippines and a leader of the Philippine Revolution.

name: Emilio Segrè
overview: Emilio Segrè was an Italian-American physicist who discovered the antiproton and technetium, the first artificially produced element.

name: Emily Brontë
overview: Emily Brontë was an English novelist and poet who is best known for her only novel, Wuthering Heights, considered a classic of English literature.

name: Emily Dickinson
overview: Emily Dickinson was an American poet who wrote nearly 1,800 poems, most published posthumously. Her innovative use of form, punctuation, and imagery made her one of America's greatest poets.

name: Emmeline Pankhurst
overview: Emmeline Pankhurst was a British political activist who organized the suffragette movement and helped women win the right to vote.

name: Emmy Noether
overview: Emmy Noether was a German mathematician who made groundbreaking contributions to abstract algebra and theoretical physics. Noether's theorem connects symmetries and conservation laws.

name: Emmy Noether
overview: Emmy Noether was a German mathematician who made groundbreaking contributions to abstract algebra and theoretical physics. Her most famous result, Noether's theorem, establishes a profound connection between symmetries and conservation laws in physics. Einstein described her as the most important woman in the history of mathematics.

name: Enrico Caruso
overview: Enrico Caruso was an Italian operatic tenor who became the first major recording star and one of the most famous singers in history.

name: Enrico Fermi
overview: Enrico Fermi was an Italian-American physicist known for creating the first nuclear reactor and for his contributions to quantum theory, nuclear and particle physics, and statistical mechanics. He was one of the few physicists who excelled in both theory and experiment. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1938.

name: E.O. Wilson
overview: Edward O. Wilson was an American biologist and naturalist known as the father of sociobiology and a champion of biodiversity conservation.

name: Epictetus
overview: Epictetus was a Greek Stoic philosopher who was born a slave and became one of the most influential teachers of Stoic ethics in the Roman Empire.

name: Epicurus
overview: Epicurus was an ancient Greek philosopher who founded Epicureanism, a philosophy advocating the pursuit of modest pleasures, friendship, and freedom from fear as the path to happiness.

name: Desiderius Erasmus
overview: Desiderius Erasmus was a Dutch Renaissance humanist, Catholic priest, and theologian. He was the most famous scholar of his time and a leading figure of Christian humanism.

name: Eric Cornell
overview: Eric Cornell, with Carl Wieman, first achieved Bose-Einstein condensation in a dilute gas.

name: Ernest Hemingway
overview: Ernest Hemingway was an American novelist and journalist whose spare, understated prose style influenced 20th-century fiction. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954.

name: Ernest Rutherford
overview: Ernest Rutherford was a New Zealand-born British physicist who is considered the father of nuclear physics. He discovered the atomic nucleus, proposed the nuclear model of the atom, and performed the first artificial nuclear reaction.

name: Ernst Haeckel
overview: Ernst Haeckel was a German biologist, naturalist, and artist who named thousands of new species, mapped a genealogical tree of life, and coined terms including 'ecology' and 'phylogeny.'

name: Ernst Kummer
overview: Ernst Kummer was a German mathematician who introduced ideal numbers and made important contributions to number theory and algebraic geometry.

name: Ernst Mayr
overview: Ernst Mayr was a German-American biologist who was one of the 20th century's leading evolutionary biologists, known for the biological species concept.

name: Erwin Schrödinger
overview: Erwin Schrödinger was an Austrian physicist who developed wave mechanics, a fundamental formulation of quantum mechanics. He is best known for the Schrödinger equation and his famous thought experiment, Schrödinger's cat. He shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Paul Dirac.

name: Euclid
overview: Euclid was an ancient Greek mathematician often referred to as the father of geometry. His work Elements is one of the most influential texts in the history of mathematics.

name: Eugene Wigner
overview: Eugene Wigner was a Hungarian-American theoretical physicist who made fundamental contributions to quantum mechanics and nuclear physics through the application of group theory. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1963 for his work on the theory of the atomic nucleus and elementary particles.

name: Euripides
overview: Euripides was the most modern of the three great Athenian tragedians, known for realistic characters and questioning traditional values.

name: Eva Peron
overview: Eva Peron, known as Evita, was the First Lady of Argentina and a powerful political figure who championed workers' rights and women's suffrage.

name: Evangelista Torricelli
overview: Evangelista Torricelli was an Italian physicist and mathematician who invented the barometer and demonstrated the existence of atmospheric pressure and the vacuum. He also made important contributions to mathematics, including the discovery of Torricelli's trumpet, a shape with finite volume but infinite surface area.

name: Évariste Galois
overview: Évariste Galois was a French mathematician who founded group theory and Galois theory, establishing conditions under which polynomial equations can be solved. He died in a duel at age 20.

name: Ezra Pound
overview: Ezra Pound was an expatriate American poet and critic who was a driving force behind literary modernism.

name: Faith Ringgold
overview: Faith Ringgold was an American artist, author, and activist best known for her painted story quilts that addressed race, gender, and American identity.

name: Fela Kuti
overview: Fela Kuti was a Nigerian multi-instrumentalist, musician, composer, and political activist who pioneered Afrobeat, fusing traditional Yoruba music with jazz and funk.

name: Felix Hausdorff
overview: Felix Hausdorff was a pioneer of topology and set theory who introduced the concept of Hausdorff spaces and fractal dimension.

name: Felix Klein
overview: Felix Klein was a German mathematician known for his work in group theory, complex analysis, non-Euclidean geometry, and the Erlangen program classifying geometries by their symmetry groups.

name: Felix Mendelssohn
overview: Felix Mendelssohn was a German composer, pianist, and conductor of the early Romantic period, known for reviving interest in Bach's music.

name: Ferdinand de Lesseps
overview: Ferdinand de Lesseps was a French diplomat and entrepreneur who supervised the construction of the Suez Canal, one of the greatest engineering feats of the 19th century.

name: Ferdinand de Saussure
overview: Ferdinand de Saussure was a Swiss linguist whose ideas on the structure of language founded modern structural linguistics and influenced the entire field of semiotics.

name: Ferdinand Magellan
overview: Ferdinand Magellan organized the first circumnavigation of the Earth.

name: Ferdinand Marcos
overview: Ferdinand Marcos was the president of the Philippines who imposed martial law and was overthrown by a people's revolution.

name: Ferdinand von Zeppelin
overview: Ferdinand von Zeppelin was a German general and aircraft manufacturer who developed the rigid airship that bears his name.

name: Ferdowsi
overview: Ferdowsi was the author of the Shahnameh, the Persian national epic, which preserved Persian identity after the Arab conquest.

name: Fibonacci
overview: Fibonacci, also known as Leonardo of Pisa, was an Italian mathematician who popularized the Hindu-Arabic numeral system in Europe and discovered the Fibonacci sequence.

name: Fidel Castro
overview: Fidel Castro was a Cuban revolutionary and politician who served as Prime Minister and President of Cuba for nearly fifty years.

name: Filippo Brunelleschi
overview: Brunelleschi was the founding father of Renaissance architecture who engineered the dome of Florence Cathedral, a feat deemed impossible.

name: Florence Nightingale
overview: Florence Nightingale was the founder of modern nursing who transformed hospital sanitation and established nursing as a respected profession.

name: Frances Arnold
overview: Frances Arnold is an American chemical engineer and Nobel laureate who pioneered the use of directed evolution to engineer enzymes.

name: Francis Bacon
overview: Francis Bacon was an English philosopher and statesman who developed the empirical method and is considered the father of empiricism and the scientific method.

name: Francis Collins
overview: Francis Collins is an American physician-geneticist who led the Human Genome Project and later served as director of the National Institutes of Health.

name: Francis Crick
overview: Francis Crick was a British molecular biologist, biophysicist, and neuroscientist who co-discovered the structure of DNA and later proposed the central dogma of molecular biology.

name: Francis Galton
overview: Francis Galton was an English polymath who pioneered the use of statistical methods in biology, developed fingerprint identification, and founded the study of human heredity.

name: Francisco Goya
overview: Francisco Goya was a Spanish painter and printmaker regarded as the last of the Old Masters and the first of the moderns.

name: François Mitterrand
overview: François Mitterrand was the longest-serving President of France, who modernized the country and deepened European integration.

name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
overview: Franklin D. Roosevelt was the 32nd President of the United States who led the country through the Great Depression and most of World War II.

name: Frantz Fanon
overview: Frantz Fanon was a Martinican-French psychiatrist and political philosopher whose works on the psychopathology of colonization and decolonization influenced liberation movements worldwide.

name: Franz Kafka
overview: Franz Kafka was a German-speaking Bohemian novelist whose surreal and nightmarish works explore alienation, bureaucracy, and existential anxiety. The word 'Kafkaesque' derives from his vision.

name: Franz Liszt
overview: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and virtuoso pianist who was one of the most celebrated musicians of the 19th century.

name: Franz Schubert
overview: Franz Schubert was an Austrian composer of the late Classical and early Romantic eras, known especially for his prolific output of lieder and chamber music.

name: Fred Hoyle
overview: Fred Hoyle was a British astronomer who formulated the theory of stellar nucleosynthesis and controversially promoted the steady-state model of the universe.

name: Freddie Mercury
overview: Freddie Mercury was a British singer-songwriter and the lead vocalist of Queen, widely regarded as one of the greatest rock singers of all time.

name: Frédéric Chopin
overview: Frédéric Chopin was a Polish composer and virtuoso pianist of the Romantic era who wrote primarily for solo piano.

name: Linus Pauling's student Ahmed Hassan Zewail
overview: Frédéric Joliot-Curie was a French physicist who, with his wife Irène, received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the discovery of artificial radioactivity.

name: Frederick Douglass
overview: Frederick Douglass was an American social reformer, abolitionist, orator, writer, and statesman who became the most prominent spokesperson for abolition.

name: Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor
overview: Frederick II was a Holy Roman Emperor called Stupor Mundi (Wonder of the World) for his extraordinary learning and ambition.

name: Frederick Reines
overview: Frederick Reines was an American physicist who first detected the neutrino, confirming a particle predicted 26 years earlier by Pauli.

name: Frederick Sanger
overview: Frederick Sanger was a British biochemist who won two Nobel Prizes in Chemistry for his work on protein and DNA sequencing.

name: Freeman Dyson
overview: Freeman Dyson was a British-American theoretical physicist and mathematician who unified the competing formulations of quantum electrodynamics by Schwinger, Tomonaga, and Feynman. He made wide-ranging contributions to physics, mathematics, and futuristic engineering concepts.

name: Frida Kahlo
overview: Frida Kahlo was a Mexican painter known for her self-portraits, works inspired by Mexican folk art, and her exploration of identity, pain, and the human body.

name: Friedrich Nietzsche
overview: Friedrich Nietzsche was a German philosopher whose radical ideas on morality, religion, and the will to power profoundly influenced 20th-century thought.

name: Friedrich Schelling
overview: Friedrich Schelling was a central figure in German idealism who developed a philosophy of nature and art.

name: Friedrich Wöhler
overview: Friedrich Wöhler was a German chemist who is best known for his synthesis of urea, the first organic compound produced from inorganic materials, disproving vitalism.

name: Fritz Haber
overview: Fritz Haber was a German chemist who received the Nobel Prize for synthesizing ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen, enabling industrial fertilizer production that feeds billions.

name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
overview: Fyodor Dostoevsky was a Russian novelist and philosopher whose psychological depth and exploration of the human condition make him one of the greatest novelists in world literature.

name: Fyodor Tyutchev
overview: Fyodor Tyutchev was a Russian poet and diplomat considered one of the three greatest Russian poets alongside Pushkin and Lermontov. His philosophical lyrics explore nature and the cosmos.

name: G.H. Hardy
overview: G.H. Hardy was an English mathematician known for his work in number theory and mathematical analysis, and for his collaboration with Ramanujan.

name: Gabriel García Márquez
overview: Gabriel García Márquez was a Colombian novelist and Nobel laureate who was the foremost practitioner of magical realism. One Hundred Years of Solitude is one of the most significant novels of the 20th century.

name: Gabriela Mistral
overview: Gabriela Mistral was a Chilean poet, diplomat, and educator who was the first Latin American author to receive a Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Galen
overview: Galen was a Greek physician and philosopher whose medical theories dominated Western medicine for over 1,300 years.

name: Galileo Galilei
overview: Galileo Galilei was an Italian astronomer, physicist, and mathematician, often called the father of modern observational astronomy and modern physics. His improvements to the telescope and consequent astronomical observations supported the Copernican heliocentric model.

name: Gamal Abdel Nasser
overview: Gamal Abdel Nasser was the second President of Egypt and the leading figure of Arab nationalism who transformed Egypt and inspired anti-colonial movements across the Middle East.

name: Genghis Khan
overview: Genghis Khan was the founder and first ruler of the Mongol Empire, which became the largest contiguous land empire in history.

name: Georg Cantor
overview: Georg Cantor was a German mathematician who created set theory and established the concept of infinite numbers. His work proved that infinities come in different sizes.

name: Georg Ohm
overview: Georg Simon Ohm was a German physicist and mathematician who discovered the fundamental law governing electrical resistance. Ohm's law, relating voltage, current, and resistance, is one of the most basic and important laws in electrical science.

name: Georg Philipp Telemann
overview: Telemann was the most prolific major composer in history, whose works bridged the late Baroque and early Classical styles.

name: Georg Simmel
overview: Georg Simmel was a German sociologist and philosopher who pioneered the study of social interaction, urban life, and the philosophy of money.

name: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
overview: Hegel was a German philosopher who developed a comprehensive philosophical framework based on dialectics. His ideas on history, spirit, and the state profoundly influenced Western philosophy.

name: George Beadle
overview: George Beadle was an American geneticist who won the Nobel Prize for demonstrating that genes act through the production of enzymes — the one gene-one enzyme hypothesis.

name: George Boole
overview: George Boole was an English mathematician and logician who developed Boolean algebra, the basis for modern digital computer circuits and programming.

name: George Frideric Handel
overview: George Frideric Handel was a German-born British Baroque composer known for his operas, oratorios, anthems, and organ concertos.

name: George Gamow
overview: George Gamow was a Ukrainian-American theoretical physicist and cosmologist who proposed the Big Bang nucleosynthesis theory. He also made important contributions to nuclear physics, molecular biology, and science popularization.

name: George Gershwin
overview: George Gershwin was an American composer and pianist whose compositions spanned popular music, jazz, and classical forms.

name: George Pólya
overview: George Pólya was a Hungarian mathematician known for his work in combinatorics and mathematical pedagogy.

name: George Pullman
overview: George Pullman was an American industrialist who revolutionized rail travel by developing the luxury sleeping car and founding the Pullman Palace Car Company.

name: George Stephenson
overview: George Stephenson was the 'Father of Railways' who built the first public inter-city railway line and established the standard gauge used worldwide.

name: George Washington Carver
overview: George Washington Carver was an American agricultural scientist who developed hundreds of products from peanuts, sweet potatoes, and soybeans.

name: George Washington
overview: George Washington was the first President of the United States and commander-in-chief of the Continental Army during the American Revolution.

name: George Westinghouse
overview: George Westinghouse was an American entrepreneur and engineer who championed alternating current and made railroad travel safer.

name: Georges Cuvier
overview: Georges Cuvier was a French naturalist and zoologist who established the fields of comparative anatomy and paleontology and proved that extinction was a real phenomenon.

name: Georges Lemaître
overview: Georges Lemaître was a Belgian priest and physicist who first proposed the Big Bang theory of the origin of the universe.

name: Georgia O'Keeffe
overview: Georgia O'Keeffe was an American artist known for her paintings of enlarged flowers, New York skyscrapers, and New Mexico landscapes, recognized as the Mother of American Modernism.

name: Gerhard Domagk
overview: Gerhard Domagk was a German pathologist and bacteriologist who discovered sulfonamide, the first commercially available antibiotic, saving millions of lives.

name: Gerhard Ertl
overview: Gerhard Ertl is a German physicist and physical chemist who won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his studies of chemical processes on solid surfaces.

name: Alexander Fleming's contemporary Gertrude Elion
overview: Gertrude Elion was an American pharmacologist and biochemist who shared the Nobel Prize for pioneering a rational approach to drug development.

name: Getulio Vargas
overview: Getulio Vargas was the longest-serving President of Brazil who modernized the country's economy and labor system during the Estado Novo era.

name: Giacomo Puccini
overview: Giacomo Puccini was an Italian opera composer who was the last great representative of the Italian operatic tradition.

name: Giambattista Vico
overview: Giambattista Vico was an Italian philosopher who pioneered the philosophy of history.

name: Gilbert N. Lewis
overview: Gilbert N. Lewis was an American physical chemist known for the discovery of the covalent bond, Lewis dot structures, and his concept of acids and bases.

name: Giordano Bruno
overview: Giordano Bruno was an Italian philosopher and cosmological theorist who proposed that the universe is infinite and contains many worlds. He was burned at the stake for heresy.

name: Giotto di Bondone
overview: Giotto was the founder of the central tradition of Western painting, breaking from Byzantine formalism to depict natural human emotion.

name: Giovanni Cassini
overview: Giovanni Cassini was an Italian-French astronomer who discovered four of Saturn's moons and the gap in Saturn's rings that bears his name.

name: Giulio Natta
overview: Giulio Natta was an Italian chemist who won the Nobel Prize for his work on high polymers, developing stereospecific polymerization to create isotactic polypropylene.

name: Giuseppe Garibaldi
overview: Giuseppe Garibaldi was an Italian general and patriot who played a major role in the unification of Italy.

name: Giuseppe Peano
overview: Giuseppe Peano was an Italian mathematician who made foundational contributions to mathematical logic and set theory, including the Peano axioms for natural numbers.

name: Giuseppe Verdi
overview: Giuseppe Verdi was an Italian opera composer who dominated Italian opera for half a century, creating works of dramatic power and emotional depth.

name: Glenn T. Seaborg
overview: Glenn Seaborg was an American chemist who won the Nobel Prize for discoveries in the chemistry of transuranium elements. He identified or co-discovered ten elements.

name: Johann Gottfried Herder
overview: Johann Gottfried Herder was a German philosopher, theologian, and literary critic who was a major figure in the Counter-Enlightenment and a founder of cultural nationalism.

name: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
overview: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was a German polymath who independently invented calculus, developed binary number systems, and made contributions to logic and philosophy.

name: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
overview: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was a German polymath who independently developed calculus and made major contributions to philosophy, logic, and mechanical calculation.

name: Gottlieb Daimler
overview: Gottlieb Daimler was a German engineer and industrialist who pioneered the high-speed internal combustion engine and the modern automobile.

name: Grace Hopper
overview: Grace Hopper was an American computer scientist and United States Navy rear admiral who was a pioneer of computer programming.

name: Gregor Mendel
overview: Gregor Mendel was an Augustinian friar and scientist who discovered the fundamental laws of inheritance through his experiments with pea plants.

name: Grigori Perelman
overview: Grigori Perelman is a Russian mathematician who proved the Poincaré conjecture and Thurston's geometrization conjecture, two of the most important problems in topology.

name: Guglielmo Marconi
overview: Guglielmo Marconi was an Italian inventor and electrical engineer who pioneered long-distance radio transmission. He shared the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics for his contributions to the development of wireless telegraphy, which revolutionized global communications.

name: Guru Nanak
overview: Guru Nanak was the founder of Sikhism and the first of the ten Sikh Gurus.

name: Gustav Hertz
overview: Gustav Hertz, with James Franck, performed the Franck-Hertz experiment confirming quantized energy levels in atoms.

name: Gustav Kirchhoff
overview: Gustav Kirchhoff was a German physicist who formulated fundamental laws governing electrical circuits and co-founded the science of spectroscopy. His circuit laws remain essential tools in electrical engineering and physics.

name: Gustav Klimt
overview: Gustav Klimt was an Austrian symbolist painter and one of the most prominent members of the Vienna Secession movement, known for his ornamental, gold-leaf paintings.

name: Gustav Mahler
overview: Gustav Mahler was an Austrian-Bohemian late-Romantic composer and conductor, known for his monumental symphonies and song cycles.

name: Gustave Courbet
overview: Gustave Courbet was a French painter who led the Realist movement in 19th-century art, rejecting Romanticism in favor of depicting ordinary life.

name: Gustave Eiffel
overview: Gustave Eiffel was a French civil engineer who designed the Eiffel Tower and the internal structure of the Statue of Liberty.

name: Gustave Flaubert
overview: Gustave Flaubert was a French novelist considered one of the most influential Western novelists, known for his meticulous literary style.

name: Gwendolyn Brooks
overview: Gwendolyn Brooks was the first African American to win the Pulitzer Prize.

name: Hafez
overview: Hafez was the greatest Persian lyric poet, whose ghazals are memorized and recited throughout the Persian-speaking world.

name: Haile Selassie
overview: Haile Selassie was the Emperor of Ethiopia from 1930 to 1974, a major figure in African politics, and is revered as the messiah in the Rastafari movement.

name: Hammurabi
overview: Hammurabi was the sixth king of the First Babylonian Dynasty, famous for one of the earliest known written legal codes.

name: Hannah Arendt
overview: Hannah Arendt was a German-American political theorist whose works on totalitarianism, the nature of power, and the banality of evil are among the most important in 20th-century political thought.

name: Hannibal Barca
overview: Hannibal Barca was Carthage's greatest general, famous for crossing the Alps with elephants and nearly conquering Rome.

name: Hans Bethe
overview: Hans Bethe was a German-American nuclear physicist who won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1967 for his work on stellar nucleosynthesis. He explained the nuclear reactions that power the sun and stars, and also made major contributions to quantum electrodynamics and solid-state physics.

name: Hans Christian Andersen
overview: Hans Christian Andersen was a Danish author known for his fairy tales.

name: Hans Dehmelt
overview: Hans Dehmelt developed the ion trap technique, enabling precision measurements of individual particles.

name: Har Gobind Khorana
overview: Har Gobind Khorana shared the Nobel Prize for deciphering the genetic code and synthesizing the first artificial gene.

name: Harold Urey
overview: Harold Urey was an American physical chemist who discovered deuterium and pioneered the study of the origin of life.

name: Harriet Tubman
overview: Harriet Tubman was an American abolitionist who escaped from slavery and made thirteen missions to rescue approximately seventy enslaved people using the Underground Railroad.

name: Harry S. Truman
overview: Harry Truman was the 33rd President of the United States who made the decision to use atomic weapons and implemented the Marshall Plan.

name: Harsha
overview: Emperor Harsha of Kannauj was one of the last great rulers of ancient India, known for his patronage of arts and Buddhism.

name: Haruki Murakami
overview: Haruki Murakami is a Japanese novelist whose surreal, melancholic fiction blends Western and Japanese literary traditions. He is one of the most widely read contemporary authors.

name: Hatshepsut
overview: Hatshepsut was one of the most successful pharaohs of ancient Egypt, ruling as regent and then pharaoh during one of Egypt's most prosperous periods.

name: Hector Berlioz
overview: Hector Berlioz was a French Romantic composer who was a major innovator in orchestration and the inventor of the program symphony.

name: Hedy Lamarr
overview: Hedy Lamarr was an Austrian-American actress and inventor who co-developed a radio guidance system using frequency-hopping spread spectrum technology.

name: Heinrich Hertz
overview: Heinrich Hertz was a German physicist who first conclusively proved the existence of electromagnetic waves predicted by Maxwell's theory. His experiments demonstrated that electromagnetic waves travel at the speed of light and can be reflected, refracted, and polarized.

name: Helmut Kohl
overview: Helmut Kohl was a German Chancellor who presided over the reunification of Germany and was a driving force behind European integration.

name: Hendrik Lorentz
overview: Hendrik Lorentz was a Dutch physicist who developed the Lorentz transformation equations and the electron theory of matter. He shared the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physics and his mathematical framework became essential to Einstein's special theory of relativity.

name: Henri Becquerel
overview: Henri Becquerel was a French physicist who discovered radioactivity in 1896, a finding that fundamentally changed our understanding of matter and energy. He shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with Pierre and Marie Curie for this groundbreaking work.

name: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec
overview: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec was a French painter, printmaker, draughtsman, and illustrator whose art depicted the colorful and theatrical life of Paris.

name: Henri Matisse
overview: Henri Matisse was a French visual artist known for his use of color and his fluid, original draughtsmanship. He was a leading figure of Fauvism.

name: Henri Poincaré
overview: Henri Poincaré was a French mathematician, physicist, and philosopher of science who made fundamental contributions to topology, celestial mechanics, and the theory of dynamical systems.

name: Henrietta Swan Leavitt
overview: Henrietta Swan Leavitt was an American astronomer who discovered the period-luminosity relationship of Cepheid variables, enabling measurement of cosmic distances.

name: Henry Cavendish
overview: Henry Cavendish was an English natural philosopher and chemist who discovered hydrogen, determined the composition of water, and measured the density of the Earth.

name: Henry Ford
overview: Henry Ford was an American industrialist and founder of the Ford Motor Company who pioneered the assembly line method of mass production.

name: Heraclitus
overview: Heraclitus of Ephesus proposed that change is the fundamental nature of the universe, symbolized by ever-living fire.

name: Herbert Spencer
overview: Herbert Spencer was an English philosopher and sociologist who developed an all-encompassing evolutionary philosophy and coined the phrase 'survival of the fittest.'

name: Hermann Hesse
overview: Hermann Hesse was a German-Swiss poet, novelist, and painter who won the Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Herman Melville
overview: Herman Melville was an American novelist and poet best known for Moby-Dick, one of the great masterpieces of American literature.

name: Hermann Staudinger
overview: Hermann Staudinger was a German organic chemist who demonstrated the existence of macromolecules, founding polymer chemistry and winning the Nobel Prize.

name: Hermann von Helmholtz
overview: Hermann von Helmholtz was a German physicist and physician who made fundamental contributions to the conservation of energy, optics, electrodynamics, and the physiology of perception. He was one of the most versatile scientists of the 19th century.

name: Hermann Weyl
overview: Hermann Weyl was a German mathematician and physicist who made major contributions to group theory, differential geometry, and quantum mechanics.

name: Herodotus
overview: Herodotus is called the Father of History for his systematic investigation of the Greco-Persian Wars and the cultures he encountered.

name: Hideki Yukawa
overview: Hideki Yukawa was a Japanese theoretical physicist who predicted the existence of mesons as the carriers of the nuclear force. He became the first Japanese person to receive the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1949. His work was fundamental to the development of nuclear and particle physics.

name: Hildegard von Bingen
overview: Hildegard von Bingen was a German Benedictine abbess, writer, composer, and polymath, one of the most remarkable women of the medieval period.

name: Hippocrates
overview: Hippocrates was an ancient Greek physician known as the 'Father of Medicine' who established medicine as a discipline separate from philosophy and superstition.

name: Ho Chi Minh
overview: Ho Chi Minh was a Vietnamese revolutionary and statesman who served as Prime Minister and President of North Vietnam.

name: Homer
overview: Homer was an ancient Greek poet traditionally credited as the author of the Iliad and the Odyssey, the foundational works of Western literature.

name: Homi J. Bhabha
overview: Homi Jehangir Bhabha was an Indian nuclear physicist who played a central role in establishing India's nuclear program. He made significant contributions to the theory of cosmic radiation and electron-positron scattering, and founded both the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and India's Atomic Energy Commission.

name: Horace
overview: Horace was one of Rome's greatest lyric poets, whose Odes, Satires, and Epistles set standards for Western poetry.

name: Howard Florey
overview: Howard Florey was an Australian pharmacologist who led the team that developed penicillin for clinical use, sharing the Nobel Prize.

name: Hugh Everett III
overview: Hugh Everett III was an American physicist who proposed the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics, suggesting that all possible quantum outcomes are physically realized in branching parallel universes. Though initially dismissed, his interpretation has become one of the most discussed foundations of quantum theory.

name: Humphry Davy
overview: Humphry Davy was a Cornish chemist and inventor who isolated several chemical elements using electrolysis, including sodium, potassium, calcium, and barium.

name: Hypatia
overview: Hypatia of Alexandria was a Greek mathematician, astronomer, and philosopher. She is the first female mathematician whose life and work are reasonably well recorded.

name: Ibn al-Haytham
overview: Ibn al-Haytham, known in the West as Alhazen, was an Arab mathematician, astronomer, and physicist who is widely considered the father of modern optics. His Book of Optics fundamentally changed the understanding of light and vision.

name: Ibn Battuta
