overview: Sergei Rachmaninoff was a Russian composer, virtuoso pianist, and conductor of the late Romantic era.

name: Shaka Zulu
overview: Shaka Zulu was the founder of the Zulu Kingdom and a military innovator who transformed warfare in southern Africa.

name: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
overview: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was the founding father of Bangladesh and its first president.

name: Sheldon Glashow
overview: Sheldon Glashow is an American theoretical physicist who made foundational contributions to the electroweak unification of the electromagnetic and weak nuclear forces. He shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics with Abdus Salam and Steven Weinberg for this work.

name: Shiing-Shen Chern
overview: Shiing-Shen Chern was a Chinese-American mathematician who made fundamental contributions to differential geometry and topology, including the Chern classes.

name: Sin-Itiro Tomonaga
overview: Sin-Itiro Tomonaga was a Japanese physicist who shared the Nobel Prize for fundamental work in quantum electrodynamics.

name: Shotoku Taishi
overview: Prince Shotoku was a semi-legendary regent of Japan who promoted Buddhism and Chinese political institutions, shaping the foundations of Japanese civilization.

name: Siméon Denis Poisson
overview: Poisson made fundamental contributions to mathematical physics, probability theory, and pure mathematics.

name: Simón Bolívar
overview: Simón Bolívar was a Venezuelan military and political leader who played a key role in the independence of several South American countries from the Spanish Empire.

name: Simon van der Meer
overview: Simon van der Meer was a Dutch accelerator physicist who developed stochastic cooling, enabling the discovery of the W and Z bosons.

name: Simone de Beauvoir
overview: Simone de Beauvoir was a French existentialist philosopher and feminist writer. Her book The Second Sex is a foundational text of modern feminism.

name: Simone Weil
overview: Simone Weil was a French philosopher, mystic, and political activist whose writings on attention, affliction, and grace are among the most profound of the 20th century.

name: Sin-Itiro Tomonaga
overview: Sin-Itiro Tomonaga was a Japanese theoretical physicist who shared the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physics for his independent development of quantum electrodynamics. Working largely in isolation in wartime Japan, he developed a relativistically covariant formulation of QED.

name: Sirimavo Bandaranaike
overview: Sirimavo Bandaranaike was the world's first female prime minister.

name: Socrates
overview: Socrates was an ancient Greek philosopher credited as the founder of Western philosophy. He developed the Socratic method of questioning to stimulate critical thinking.

name: Sofia Kovalevskaya
overview: Sofia Kovalevskaya was a Russian mathematician who was the first woman to obtain a doctorate in mathematics and the first woman appointed to a full professorship in Europe.

name: Sophie Germain
overview: Sophie Germain was a French mathematician who made important contributions to number theory and elasticity theory, working in an era when women were excluded from formal scientific education.

name: Sophocles
overview: Sophocles was one of the three great tragedians of classical Athens, known for masterful character development and dramatic irony.

name: Sophus Lie
overview: Sophus Lie created the theory of continuous transformation groups, now called Lie groups, fundamental to modern mathematics and physics.

name: Sor Juana Ines de la Cruz
overview: Sor Juana Ines de la Cruz was a Mexican nun, scholar, and poet considered the greatest literary figure of colonial Latin America.

name: Søren Kierkegaard
overview: Søren Kierkegaard was a Danish philosopher, theologian, and cultural critic, widely considered the first existentialist philosopher.

name: Srinivasa Ramanujan
overview: Srinivasa Ramanujan was an Indian mathematician who made extraordinary contributions to number theory, infinite series, and continued fractions, largely self-taught and working in isolation.

name: Stanislao Cannizzaro
overview: Stanislao Cannizzaro was an Italian chemist who revived Avogadro's hypothesis and established a consistent system of atomic weights that unified chemistry.

name: Stefan Banach
overview: Stefan Banach was a Polish mathematician and one of the founders of functional analysis. Banach spaces, named after him, are fundamental objects in modern analysis.

name: Stéphane Mallarmé
overview: Stéphane Mallarmé was a French poet and critic, a major figure in Symbolism.

name: Stephen Hawking
overview: Stephen Hawking was a British theoretical physicist and cosmologist known for his groundbreaking work on black holes and general relativity. His discovery that black holes emit radiation, now called Hawking radiation, transformed the understanding of quantum gravity and made him one of the most famous scientists in history.

name: Stephen Jay Gould
overview: Stephen Jay Gould was an American paleontologist and evolutionary biologist who proposed the theory of punctuated equilibrium and was a prolific popular science writer.

name: Steve Wozniak
overview: Steve Wozniak is an American electronics engineer and programmer who co-founded Apple Computer and designed the Apple I and Apple II.

name: Steven Weinberg
overview: Steven Weinberg was an American theoretical physicist who unified the electromagnetic and weak nuclear forces into the electroweak interaction. He shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics and was considered one of the most influential physicists of the late 20th century.

name: Subhas Chandra Bose
overview: Subhas Chandra Bose was an Indian nationalist leader who sought independence through armed struggle.

name: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar
overview: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar was an Indian-American astrophysicist known for determining the mass limit for white dwarf stars, now called the Chandrasekhar limit. His work laid the foundation for the modern theory of stellar evolution. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1983.

name: Suharto
overview: Suharto was the second president of Indonesia, ruling for 31 years during the New Order era.

name: Sukarno
overview: Sukarno was the first president of Indonesia and a leader of the Indonesian independence movement.

name: Suleiman the Magnificent
overview: Suleiman the Magnificent was the tenth and longest-reigning Sultan of the Ottoman Empire, during which it reached the peak of its power.

name: Sun Tzu
overview: Sun Tzu was a Chinese military strategist, philosopher, and author of The Art of War, one of the most influential treatises on military strategy.

name: Sun Yat-sen
overview: Sun Yat-sen was a Chinese revolutionary and political leader who is considered the father of modern China for his role in overthrowing the Qing dynasty.

name: Sundiata Keita
overview: Sundiata Keita was the founder of the Mali Empire and is celebrated as one of the greatest heroes of West African history.

name: Suryavarman II
overview: Suryavarman II was the Khmer king who built Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument in the world.

name: Svante Arrhenius
overview: Svante Arrhenius was a Swedish scientist who received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his electrolytic theory of dissociation. He was also an early researcher of the greenhouse effect.

name: Sviatoslav Richter
overview: Sviatoslav Richter was a Ukrainian-born Soviet pianist renowned for his immense repertoire, technical power, and profound interpretive depth.

name: Sydney Brenner
overview: Sydney Brenner was a South African biologist who won the Nobel Prize for discoveries about genetic regulation of organ development and programmed cell death.

name: Sylvia Plath
overview: Sylvia Plath was an American poet and novelist whose confessional poetry explored identity, suffering, and death.

name: Syngman Rhee
overview: Syngman Rhee was the first president of South Korea and a lifelong independence activist.

name: Takashi Murakami
overview: Takashi Murakami is a Japanese contemporary artist who blurs the boundary between high and low culture.

name: Takeda Shingen
overview: Takeda Shingen was a powerful daimyo of Kai Province, famous for his innovative cavalry tactics and his rivalry with Uesugi Kenshin.

name: Charles Maurice de Talleyrand
overview: Talleyrand was a French diplomat who served every regime from the Ancien Régime through the Bourbon Restoration, shaping European diplomacy.

name: Tamara de Lempicka
overview: Tamara de Lempicka was a Polish painter who was the most prominent Art Deco painter, famous for her polished portraits of the wealthy and fashionable.

name: Tamerlane
overview: Tamerlane was a Turco-Mongol conqueror who founded the Timurid Empire spanning from Turkey to India.

name: Terence Tao
overview: Terence Tao is an Australian-American mathematician widely regarded as one of the greatest living mathematicians. He has made contributions to harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, combinatorics, and number theory.

name: Thales of Miletus
overview: Thales of Miletus is regarded as the first Western philosopher and one of the Seven Sages of Greece.

name: Thales of Miletus
overview: Thales of Miletus is widely regarded as the first Western philosopher, proposing that water is the fundamental substance of all matter.

name: Thelonious Monk
overview: Thelonious Monk was an American jazz pianist and composer, one of the founders of bebop, known for his unique improvisational style.

name: Theodor Schwann
overview: Theodor Schwann was a German physiologist who co-founded cell theory, discovered Schwann cells and pepsin, and coined the term 'metabolism.'

name: Jacobus van 't Hoff's student Wilhelm Ostwald student
overview: Theodore William Richards was an American chemist who received the Nobel Prize for his accurate determinations of the atomic weights of many chemical elements.

name: Theodore Roosevelt
overview: Theodore Roosevelt was the 26th President of the United States, known for his progressive policies, conservation efforts, and construction of the Panama Canal.

name: Theodosius Dobzhansky
overview: Theodosius Dobzhansky was a Ukrainian-American geneticist and evolutionary biologist who was a central figure in the modern evolutionary synthesis.

name: Thomas Aquinas
overview: Thomas Aquinas was an Italian Dominican friar and philosopher-theologian who synthesized Aristotelian philosophy with Christian theology. He is the most influential philosopher in the Catholic tradition.

name: Thomas Edison
overview: Thomas Edison was an American inventor and businessman who developed many devices including the phonograph, the motion picture camera, and the practical incandescent light bulb.

name: Thomas Henry Huxley
overview: Thomas Henry Huxley was an English biologist known as 'Darwin's Bulldog' for his advocacy of Charles Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection.

name: Thomas Hobbes
overview: Thomas Hobbes was an English philosopher best known for his political philosophy, particularly Leviathan, which argues for a strong sovereign authority to prevent the chaos of the state of nature.

name: Thomas Hunt Morgan
overview: Thomas Hunt Morgan was an American evolutionary biologist and geneticist who won the Nobel Prize for discoveries relating to the role of chromosomes in heredity.

name: Thomas Jefferson
overview: Thomas Jefferson was an American Founding Father, principal author of the Declaration of Independence, and the third President of the United States.

name: Thomas Mann
overview: Thomas Mann was a German novelist and Nobel laureate whose works explored bourgeois life, art, and the German condition.

name: Thomas More
overview: Thomas More was an English lawyer, philosopher, and statesman who served as Lord Chancellor under Henry VIII. His Utopia described an ideal society on a fictional island.

name: Thomas Young
overview: Thomas Young was an English polymath who made important contributions to optics, physiology, and Egyptology. He is best known for his double-slit experiment, which demonstrated the wave nature of light and established the principle of interference.

name: Thucydides
overview: Thucydides wrote the History of the Peloponnesian War, establishing rigorous standards of historical evidence and analysis.

name: Tim Berners-Lee
overview: Tim Berners-Lee is a British computer scientist who invented the World Wide Web, fundamentally changing how humanity communicates and accesses information.

name: Titian
overview: Titian was the greatest Venetian painter of the 16th century, recognized as a master of color whose work influenced generations of Western artists.

name: Tokugawa Ieyasu
overview: Tokugawa Ieyasu was the founder and first shogun of the Tokugawa shogunate of Japan, which ruled for over 260 years of peace.

name: Tokugawa Tsunayoshi
overview: Tokugawa Tsunayoshi was the fifth shogun of the Tokugawa dynasty, known for the Laws of Compassion for Living Things.

name: Tokugawa Yoshimune
overview: Tokugawa Yoshimune was the eighth shogun of the Tokugawa dynasty, known as the 'Rice Shogun' for his sweeping economic and administrative reforms.

name: Toni Morrison
overview: Toni Morrison was an American novelist who explored African American identity and history. She won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1993, the first African American woman to do so.

name: Toussaint Louverture
overview: Toussaint Louverture was the leader of the Haitian Revolution, the most successful slave revolt in history, which established Haiti as the first free Black republic.

name: Toyotomi Hideyori
overview: Toyotomi Hideyori was the son and heir of Toyotomi Hideyoshi who fought against the Tokugawa in the Siege of Osaka.

name: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
overview: Toyotomi Hideyoshi rose from peasant origins to become the second great unifier of Japan, completing the work Oda Nobunaga had begun.

name: Trajan
overview: Trajan was a Roman emperor who expanded the empire to its greatest territorial extent and was revered as the best of emperors.

name: T.S. Eliot
overview: T.S. Eliot was a modernist poet whose works defined 20th-century poetry.

name: Tsung-Dao Lee
overview: Tsung-Dao Lee was a Chinese-American physicist who shared the 1957 Nobel Prize in Physics with Chen-Ning Yang for their theoretical prediction that parity is not conserved in weak interactions. He was one of the youngest Nobel laureates in physics.

name: Tu Youyou
overview: Tu Youyou is a Chinese pharmaceutical chemist who discovered artemisinin, a drug used to treat malaria, winning the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

name: Tulsidas
overview: Tulsidas was a Hindu poet-saint best known for the Ramcharitmanas, a retelling of the Ramayana in Awadhi.

name: Tunku Abdul Rahman
overview: Tunku Abdul Rahman was the first Prime Minister of Malaya and later Malaysia, known as the Father of Independence.

name: Tycho Brahe
overview: Tycho Brahe was a Danish nobleman and astronomer who made the most precise astronomical observations of his time before the invention of the telescope.

name: Uesugi Kenshin
overview: Uesugi Kenshin was a daimyo of Echigo Province renowned as the 'God of War' and the legendary rival of Takeda Shingen during Japan's Sengoku period.

name: Umberto Eco
overview: Umberto Eco was an Italian semiotician, philosopher, and novelist whose works bridged academic semiotics and popular fiction.

name: Umm Kulthum
overview: Umm Kulthum was an Egyptian singer, songwriter, and actress who is considered the most famous and distinguished singer in the history of Arabic music.

name: Utagawa Hiroshige
overview: Utagawa Hiroshige was a Japanese ukiyo-e artist famous for his landscape series, particularly The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō.

name: Václav Havel
overview: Václav Havel was a Czech statesman, playwright, and dissident who served as the last President of Czechoslovakia and the first President of the Czech Republic.

name: Val Logsdon Fitch
overview: Val Fitch was an American nuclear physicist who co-discovered CP violation in kaon decay.

name: Vallabhbhai Patel
overview: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel unified India by integrating over 500 princely states into the Indian Union.

name: Valmiki
overview: Valmiki is revered as the first poet of Sanskrit literature and the author of the Ramayana, one of India's two great epics.

name: Vannevar Bush
overview: Vannevar Bush was an American engineer and science administrator who organized the scientific war effort during WWII and envisioned hypertext.

name: Velimir Khlebnikov
overview: Velimir Khlebnikov was a Russian poet and a founder of the Futurist movement, known for his radical linguistic experimentation.

name: Vera Rubin
overview: Vera Rubin was an American astronomer who provided some of the first strong observational evidence for the existence of dark matter. Her measurements of galaxy rotation curves showed that galaxies contain far more mass than is visible, fundamentally changing our understanding of the universe.

name: Victor Hugo
overview: Victor Hugo was a French poet, novelist, and dramatist who was the most important of the French Romantic writers. Les Misérables and The Hunchback of Notre-Dame are among the most widely read novels in world literature.

name: Vikram Sarabhai
overview: Vikram Sarabhai was the father of the Indian space program and a pioneer in applying science to national development.

name: Vincent van Gogh
overview: Vincent van Gogh was a Dutch Post-Impressionist painter who created about 2,100 artworks in roughly a decade, profoundly influencing 20th-century art.

name: Vint Cerf
overview: Vint Cerf is an American internet pioneer who is recognized as one of the fathers of the Internet for co-designing the TCP/IP protocols.

name: Virgil
overview: Virgil was an ancient Roman poet, best known for the Aeneid, the epic poem that tells the story of Rome's founding and became the definitive literary work of the Roman Empire.

name: Virginia Woolf
overview: Virginia Woolf was an English writer and modernist who pioneered the use of stream of consciousness in fiction. She is considered one of the most important authors of the 20th century.

name: Vladimir Horowitz
overview: Vladimir Horowitz was a Ukrainian-born American pianist regarded as one of the greatest pianists of all time.

name: Voltaire
overview: Voltaire was a French Enlightenment writer, philosopher, and satirist known for his wit, his advocacy of civil liberties, and his criticism of the Catholic Church.

name: Wallace Carothers
overview: Wallace Carothers was an American chemist and inventor who led pioneering work in polymer chemistry, inventing nylon and neoprene.

name: Walt Whitman
overview: Walt Whitman was an American poet whose Leaves of Grass is a landmark in American literature. His free verse and celebration of democracy, nature, and the body revolutionized poetry.

name: Walter Reed
overview: Walter Reed was an American army physician who proved that yellow fever is transmitted by mosquitoes, enabling the control of one of the most devastating tropical diseases.

name: Walther Nernst
overview: Walther Nernst was a German chemist who won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his work in thermochemistry, particularly his formulation of the third law of thermodynamics.

name: Wangari Maathai
overview: Wangari Maathai was a Kenyan environmental and political activist who founded the Green Belt Movement and became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Wassily Kandinsky
overview: Wassily Kandinsky was a Russian painter and art theorist generally credited as one of the pioneers of abstract art.

name: Werner Heisenberg
overview: Werner Heisenberg was a German theoretical physicist and a key pioneer of quantum mechanics. He formulated the uncertainty principle and developed matrix mechanics, the first complete formulation of quantum mechanics. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1932.

name: Wernher von Braun
overview: Wernher von Braun was a German-American aerospace engineer who was the chief architect of the Saturn V rocket that launched humans to the Moon.

name: W.H. Auden
overview: W.H. Auden was one of the greatest poets of the 20th century, known for his technical mastery and moral intelligence.

name: Wilhelm Ostwald
overview: Wilhelm Ostwald was a Baltic German chemist who received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his work on catalysis, chemical equilibria, and reaction velocities.

name: Wilhelm Röntgen
overview: Wilhelm Röntgen was a German physicist who discovered X-rays in 1895, a breakthrough that revolutionized medicine and earned him the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901. His discovery opened entirely new fields in medical imaging and materials science.

name: William Blake
overview: William Blake was a visionary poet, painter, and printmaker whose works combined prophetic imagination with artistic innovation.

name: William Butler Yeats
overview: W.B. Yeats was an Irish poet and one of the foremost figures of 20th-century literature.

name: William Byrd
overview: William Byrd was the greatest English composer of the Renaissance, excelling in sacred music, consort songs, and keyboard works.

name: William Faulkner
overview: William Faulkner was an American writer known for his novels set in the fictional Yoknapatawpha County, Mississippi.

name: William Gladstone
overview: William Gladstone was a British Prime Minister who served four terms and championed liberal reform, Irish Home Rule, and free trade.

name: William Harvey
overview: William Harvey was an English physician who made the first detailed description of the circulatory system, demonstrating that blood circulates through the body.

name: William Henry Perkin
overview: William Henry Perkin was a British chemist who discovered the first synthetic aniline dye, mauveine, launching the synthetic dye industry and transforming organic chemistry.

name: William Herschel
overview: William Herschel was a German-born British astronomer who discovered Uranus and made fundamental contributions to understanding the structure of the Milky Way.

name: William James
overview: William James was an American philosopher and psychologist who was a leading figure in pragmatism and the father of American psychology.

name: E.O. Wilson's Teacher William Morton Wheeler
overview: William Morton Wheeler was an American entomologist and myrmecologist who was one of the world's leading authorities on ants and social insects.

name: William of Ockham
overview: William of Ockham was a Franciscan friar and philosopher best known for Ockham's Razor.

name: William Ramsay
overview: William Ramsay was a Scottish chemist who discovered the noble gases and received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for adding an entire new group to the periodic table.

name: William Shakespeare
overview: William Shakespeare was an English playwright and poet, widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language. His plays have been translated into every major language and are performed more often than those of any other playwright.

name: William Shockley
overview: William Shockley was an American physicist who shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics for the invention of the transistor. He later invented the junction transistor, which became the basis for modern semiconductor technology.

name: William the Conqueror
overview: William the Conqueror was the Duke of Normandy who invaded England in 1066, fundamentally transforming English society and governance.

name: Willis Lamb
overview: Willis Lamb was an American physicist who discovered the Lamb shift, a small difference in energy levels of the hydrogen atom that could not be explained by the Dirac equation. This discovery was pivotal in the development of quantum electrodynamics and earned him the 1955 Nobel Prize in Physics.

name: Willy Brandt
overview: Willy Brandt was a German Chancellor whose Ostpolitik policy of engagement with Eastern Europe helped ease Cold War tensions.

name: Willy Messerschmitt
overview: Willy Messerschmitt was a German aircraft designer whose planes, particularly the Bf 109 and Me 262, were among the most significant military aircraft of the 20th century.

name: Winston Churchill
overview: Winston Churchill was a British statesman who served as Prime Minister during World War II, leading Britain through its darkest hours with resolute determination.

name: Wisława Szymborska
overview: Wisława Szymborska was a Polish poet who won the Nobel Prize in Literature for poetry that combined ironic precision with philosophical depth.

name: Wole Soyinka
overview: Wole Soyinka is a Nigerian playwright and poet who was the first African to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
overview: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was an Austrian composer who is widely regarded as among the greatest composers in the history of Western music.

name: Wolfgang Ketterle
overview: Wolfgang Ketterle achieved Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute gases of alkali atoms.

name: Wolfgang Pauli
overview: Wolfgang Pauli was an Austrian-American theoretical physicist known for his discovery of the exclusion principle, which explains the structure of atoms. He also postulated the existence of the neutrino. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1945.

name: Woodrow Wilson
overview: Woodrow Wilson was the 28th President of the United States who led the country through World War I and championed the League of Nations.

name: Orville Wright
overview: Orville Wright, together with his brother Wilbur, invented, built, and flew the first successful motor-operated airplane.

name: Wilbur Wright
overview: Wilbur Wright, together with his brother Orville, invented, built, and flew the first successful motor-operated airplane.

name: Wu Zetian
overview: Wu Zetian was the only woman in Chinese history to assume the title of Empress Regnant, ruling China during the Tang Dynasty and founding the brief Zhou Dynasty.

name: Xenophon
overview: Xenophon was an Athenian soldier, historian, and student of Socrates whose writings are major sources for Greek history and philosophy.

name: Xuanzang
overview: Xuanzang was a Chinese Buddhist monk who undertook an epic seventeen-year journey to India to obtain sacred Buddhist texts.

name: Yaa Asantewaa
overview: Yaa Asantewaa was the Queen Mother of Ejisu in the Ashanti Empire who led the final major war against British colonialism in Ghana.

name: Yasunari Kawabata
overview: Yasunari Kawabata was a Japanese novelist who was the first Japanese author to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Yayoi Kusama
overview: Yayoi Kusama is a Japanese contemporary artist known for her polka dots, infinity rooms, and immersive installations that explore infinity and self-obliteration.

name: Yevgeny Zamyatin
overview: Yevgeny Zamyatin was a Russian author best known for We, a pioneering dystopian novel that influenced Orwell's 1984 and Huxley's Brave New World.

name: Yitzhak Rabin
overview: Yitzhak Rabin was an Israeli politician and general who served as Prime Minister and signed the Oslo Accords, seeking peace with the Palestinians.

name: Yo-Yo Ma
overview: Yo-Yo Ma is a French-born American cellist known for his virtuosity, his wide-ranging musical curiosity, and his cultural ambassadorship.

name: Yoko Ono
overview: Yoko Ono is a Japanese-American artist, musician, and peace activist who was a pioneer of conceptual and performance art.

name: Yosa Buson
overview: Yosa Buson was a major Japanese poet and painter who revived the haiku tradition and is considered one of the four great haiku masters alongside Basho, Issa, and Shiki.

name: Yukio Mishima
overview: Yukio Mishima was a Japanese author nominated three times for the Nobel Prize, known for his beauty-obsessed aesthetic and dramatic death.

name: Yuri Gagarin
overview: Yuri Gagarin was a Soviet pilot and cosmonaut who became the first human in space on April 12, 1961.

name: Zaha Hadid
overview: Zaha Hadid was an Iraqi-British architect who was the first woman to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

name: Zhang Heng
overview: Zhang Heng was a Chinese polymath of the Eastern Han dynasty who made groundbreaking contributions to astronomy, mathematics, seismology, and engineering. He invented the world's first seismoscope to detect distant earthquakes and constructed a water-powered armillary sphere for astronomical observation.

name: Zheng He
overview: Zheng He was a Chinese mariner and explorer who led seven massive naval expeditions across the Indian Ocean during the Ming Dynasty.

name: Zhuangzi
overview: Zhuangzi was an ancient Chinese philosopher and one of the founders of Taoism. His eponymous book is one of the most important texts in Chinese philosophy.

name: Zora Neale Hurston
overview: Zora Neale Hurston was a novelist and anthropologist who celebrated Black Southern culture.

name: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
overview: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was the founder of the Pakistan Peoples Party and Prime Minister of Pakistan.
